newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline strengthens on U.S. stock draw.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline strengthens on U.S. stock draw.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices strengthened on the back of an unexpected draw in U.S. gasoline stocks, but apart from some light trade buying for barges business was thin, traders said.

Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute report showed a draw of 1.3 million barrels in U.S gasoline stocks and that stocks were 10.3 million barrels lower than this time last year, with implied demand running at nearly eight million barrels per day.
Today's Energy Information Administration report said gasoline stocks fell by 2.3 million barrels.
Physical barge prices jumped around $4-5 a tonne with Eurograde barges trading up to $207.75 a tonne fob ARA and regular at $200.50. Cargoes too were firmer but discussion remained muted.

Swaps climbed $3 a tonne with March swaps drifting back into a small backwardation over April. Traders said this was solely as a result of a squeeze play on spring gasoline between two trade houses. Both are thought to be running large swaps positions and have been actively buying physical barges.
March swaps were valued around $207 with April backwardated by around $1 a tonne fob ARA.
Crack spreads remained well bid around $5.50 a barrel on April with the second quarter talking $5.45.
